tasks.title: Essay: Event Sustainability Priorities
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Opinions expressed in the discussion
paragraphs: Contractor standards are the only way to ensure real change – without them, promises mean nothing.
Audience behaviour systems shift responsibility onto visitors, which is unfair and hard to enforce.
Transparent auditing builds public trust and shows the institution is serious about its commitments.

promptBlocks.text: Write an essay for your tutor discussing two of the priorities in your notes. You should explain which priority you think is more credible for an arts centre to adopt, giving reasons in support of your answer. You may, if you wish, make use of the opinions expressed in the discussion, but you should use your own words as far as possible.

tasks.title: Proposal: Sustainable-Events Framework
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: The executive board of your arts centre has decided to adopt an audited sustainable-events framework. The board has invited proposals from staff for how the framework should be implemented.

Write a proposal for the executive board. In your proposal, you should:
• recommend procurement criteria for event supplies and services
• suggest how operational ownership of sustainability targets should be assigned among staff
• outline a public reporting mechanism to demonstrate progress to stakeholders

Write your proposal.

tasks.title: Email: Supplier Negotiation
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: You are the events manager at the arts centre. The centre has just adopted a new resource policy that requires all suppliers to meet stricter environmental standards. One of your long-term suppliers, a catering company, has written to you expressing concern about the feasibility of the new requirements within the current contract period.

Write an email to the supplier. In your email, you should:
• explain the rationale behind the new policy
• acknowledge the practical constraints the supplier faces
• propose a transition timetable that balances ambition with realistic implementation

Write your email.

tasks.title: Review: Institutional Environmental Policy
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: You see this announcement in a cultural-sector journal.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted: Institutional environmental policies
paragraphs: Our journal is running a series of reviews of environmental policies adopted by cultural institutions. Have you observed or experienced the impact of such a policy at an arts centre, museum or theatre?

Write a review for our journal. In your review, evaluate the credibility of the policy's targets, assess its effect on the visitor experience, and consider whether the approach could be replicated by other cultural organisations.
